piece_title: W1-ATTR-SCALE round 1 — the attribute-scale sweep: a real 42-resolution fix resting on a root-cause claim that is false on HEAD

bifurcation.note: A numbers piece over quest data and attribute ceilings. It ships no rendered output. The one image is a chart drawn offline from the probe's own JSON and is evidence about souls awards, not about pixels.

reference_items.native_scale: five axes (consumer named, coupling measured, hand-feed audit, instrumentation honesty, harness fidelity), each 0/6/10, min-over-axes. Failure threshold: any coupling == 0 on a model the piece's own reference items require to act.
reference_items.native_verdict: 0 fail-closed — min-over-axes with an UNGATED coupling axis. The trial that carries the piece's premise had no instrument that could have failed.

checks.note: quest/machine.js:231 (resolution gates + derived faction rank ladder), engine.js:2984 _talkPersuader, character/reaction.js:83-116 (buy/sell multiplier), sim/hazards.js:297 (disease drain), sim/magic/apply.js:199-226 (restore/fortify). Perturbation moves the world: personality 10 -> 31 changes Q-BLAK-01 res_hold's refusal string.
Trials A and B are sound and genuinely coupled; --after flips them, so neither half passes alone.

UNGATED, not triggered: the trial that is supposed to establish the souls coupling has no working instrument, so no value of the coupling could have failed it. listEntities() rows carry `eid`, never `id`; `e.id !== 'player'` filters nothing and `H.killEntity(e.id)` throws every time. The builder's own shipped artifacts record five {"error":"killEntity('undefined'): no such body"} entries in BOTH arms. The verdict predicate `D.kills.every(k => k.error || k.souls_after === k.souls_before)` scores a thrown kill as a pass, and trial C is not flipped by --after, so it passes identically in both modes and would have passed forever.

The status file's finding 41 reads 'spawned dres-raid-party, killed 5 of 6 entities, stepped 60 frames each. soulsHeld 0 -> 0'. Nothing was killed. The printed line 'over 5 kill(s) of 42 entities' is counting five exceptions, and '42 entities' is the unfiltered row count (36 rows at boot in the re-run, 0 of them enemies).

No VERIFY replay existed for the consumption probe. The critic's replacement, tools/quests/critic-attr-scale-souls.mjs, supplies one and carries its own red control (sim.souls.enabled = false: 3 further kills, 0 awarded).

reference_items.why_not_ten: The one trial that establishes the piece's load-bearing premise — that killing awards no souls, so the bought attribute stream cannot be funded — killed nothing in either arm, and its predicate treats a thrown kill as a pass. Re-run with the key the harness actually returns (`eid`), 10 real kills awarded 378 souls with a red control that went red. The premise is false on HEAD.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Fix trial C: filter on `kind === 'enemy'`, use `eid`, step the world before killing (SoulsSystem.step pays only a transition it has SEEN, so spawn-then-kill-in-one-evaluate under-reads even with the right key), and make the predicate FAIL on a thrown kill rather than pass on one. Then flip it under --after like the other seven trials, so neither arm can pass alone.

reference_items.native_scale: six axes (completeness, breadth, curves, grades, two streams, six characters), each 0/6/10, min-over-axes over measurable axes. Failure threshold: any axis below 6.
reference_items.native_verdict: 0 fail-closed on the two-streams axis as the piece CALIBRATED it — not a finding against RI-PRG02's stat sheet, which has both streams

checks.value: 5 named out-of-fight consumers; attributes govern quests, ranks, persuasion, prices and disease
checks.note: This is the axis the dispatch brief flagged as the likely failure — 'a piece that made attributes purely a damage multiplier has failed the Morrowind half'. The seam attack does not land: this piece does the opposite. RI-PRG02's own 10-band asks for >=8 attributes with out-of-fight effects.

checks.value: the piece asserts the bought stream has no source; 10 kills awarded 378 souls
checks.note: The 42 rescaled demands were fitted to a ceiling of creation + earned only, on the stated premise that the bought stream is 'DEAD IN THE SHIPPED BUILD' and 'UNFUNDABLE'. game/src/sim/souls.js:321 awards 42 souls per infantry body on the alive->dead transition. In fairness: W1-SOULS wired the award path at 16:41 on 7 Aug and W1-ATTR-SCALE landed at 16:12, so the claim may have been true when written — but trial C could not have told the difference then either. SCOPE: this scores the piece's CALIBRATION, not RI-PRG02's stat sheet. The build itself has both streams and that axis passes on the build; what fails is that 42 shipped demands were fitted to a ceiling derived from only one of them.

checks.value: scalingBonus() and effectiveGrade() are called from nowhere but their own definitions
checks.note: NOT CHARGED and NOT SCORED against this piece — the unbuilt Souls half is already filed as GAP-W1-skill-and-attribute-scaling-never-reaches-damage, and this piece did not build the stat sheet. Recorded only because the round-2 successor corrected the draft's overclaim that attributes reach nothing inside the fight: they DO reach the fight through the pools (vigour->hp_max, endurance->stamina_max+regen, strength->equip_load_max, willpower->focus_max+spell_slots), and willpower reaches spell DAMAGE via engine.js:1581 -> MagicSystem.wil -> outputOf() -> combat-bridge.js:92. What is dead is WEAPON damage: inside game/src/combat/ the only attribute read of any kind is endurance -> staminaMaxFor().

reference_items.why_not_ten: Every ceiling the piece fitted to is derived from reports/faction-signature-sweep.json, which is gitignored (reports/.gitignore:3) and therefore in no commit; and the sweep moved 29 minutes after the fix landed, when W1-SOULS added a bought_points term that raised every reachable_ceiling by 2. Measured consequence: the published headline '28 defects -> 0' does not reproduce. An independent revert of the same 42 resolutions gives 23 -> 0. With bought_points folded in, the tool's RESERVE = 2 now buys ZERO margin against the earned-only ceiling for all ten attributes.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Make reports/faction-signature-sweep.json a tracked artifact (drop the ignore or move it to game/data/progression/), then replace its bought_points derivation — currently a JSON census of game/data/combat/enemies x encounters.json — with a MEASURED figure from a running world, and rescale in both directions against the corrected sweep.

reference_items.native_verdict: Mid band — the denominator is right and the label is wrong

checks.value: 370 non-violent resolutions tracked, not just 124 quests
checks.note: The builder identified and reported that the QUEST-level rate is insensitive — it does not move until the last talk route on a quest is shut — and made the resolution-level rate the headline. That judgement is correct and is the piece's best methodological call.

checks.value: '124/124 = 100.0% MEETS the 45% bar' printed from a stat-only predicate
checks.note: audit()'s `reachable` predicate looks at attribute and skill demands ONLY. knowledge, requires_knowing, disposition, items, gold and faction_rank are collected for the vacuity test and never consulted for reachability. The builder's own probe output shows a resolution counted 'reachable' that the engine refuses with 'you do not know rev_destinations | you do not know rev_meno'. 'No out-of-scale stat demand' is a useful number; it is not ARBITRATION's non-combat bar.

RI-QST05's wave-0 amendment makes PACIFIST-ALL unmeasurable without a working stealth and crime system. This piece does not claim PACIFIST-ALL; it claims stat-reachability of authored non-violent resolutions. Scored on what it claims.

reference_items.why_not_ten: The tool prints that it MEETS ARBITRATION's non-combat bar on the strength of a predicate that only knows about attribute and skill demands, so a resolution gated behind knowledge the player cannot obtain counts as reachable. W1-19-r2's critic separately measured that 0 of 35 quests behind that round's headline had a giver standing anywhere in the world.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Either extend the reachability predicate to consult knowledge, requires_knowing, disposition, items, gold and faction_rank, or relabel the printed line to what it actually measures — 'no out-of-scale stat demand on any authored non-violent resolution' — and stop citing the 45% bar from it.

ar1.not_applicable_reason: AR-1 probes the Souls half inside the fight — frames, i-frames, to-hit rolls, stamina, hitboxes. This piece touches none of them: it changes quest resolution requirement numbers in game/data/quests/** and adds an offline validator. It adds zero violent resolutions and no combat code.

checks.observed: No to-hit roll, no dice and no hit resolution anywhere in the piece's diff. The 42 edits are integers in requires.attributes and requires.skills.

The piece's whole effect is to restore non-violent exits, not remove them. Delete-the-fix measures the counterfactual directly: reverting all 42 resolutions shuts 23 authored non-violent resolutions for every character forever (370/370 -> 347/370), 19 of them shut BY a defect, and turns one quest violent-only. The fix moves the world in AR-2's direction.
No HUD, marker or compass surface is touched.

score.band_label: 0.0 fail-closed against the wave-1 gate of 7.0, by min-over-axes over an UNGATED CONSUMPTION check — NOT a judgement that the work is worthless. The 42-resolution data fix is real, wide and survives its own delete-the-fix (0 -> 23 defects, 370 -> 347 reachable on revert). The 0 records that the gate which was supposed to establish the piece's load-bearing premise had no instrument that could have fired, and the premise is false on HEAD.

biggest_gap.what: The 42 rescaled attribute and skill demands were fitted to a ceiling of creation + earned skill growth only, on the piece's stated premise that souls are never awarded and the bought attribute stream is therefore unfundable. Souls ARE awarded — 42 per infantry body, 10 real kills for 378 souls on HEAD with a red control that went red — so the true ceiling is higher and rises further as the enemy roster is populated (9 hand-placed enemies today against RI-PRG06 §7's planning figure of ~1,230). The ceilings themselves are read at run time from reports/faction-signature-sweep.json, which is gitignored and in no commit; it moved 29 minutes after the fix landed, and as a result the published headline '28 defects -> 0' re-measures as 23 -> 0. With the sweep's bought_points term folded in, the tool's RESERVE = 2 buys exactly ZERO margin against the earned-only ceiling for all ten attributes.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: Either the rank-8 social endings of three faction lines become free the moment the enemy roster lands, or they stay unreachable — and nothing in the build can currently tell which.

remedy.action: 1. Make reports/faction-signature-sweep.json a tracked artifact — drop the entry at reports/.gitignore:3 or move the file to game/data/progression/ — so every ceiling becomes a claim about a commit (rule 12). 2. Replace the sweep's bought_points derivation, currently a JSON census of game/data/combat/enemies x encounters.json, with a MEASURED figure taken from the running world by tools/quests/critic-attr-scale-souls.mjs arm 2: kill N bodies, read soulsHeld, run it through game/data/progression/levels.json. 3. Fix trial C of tools/quests/attr-scale-consumption.mjs — use `eid` not `id`, filter `kind === 'enemy'`, step the world before killing so SoulsSystem.step has SEEN the alive->dead transition, and make the predicate fail on a thrown kill rather than pass on one — then flip it under --after like the other seven trials. 4. Re-run attr-scale-audit --sheet p10 against the corrected sweep and rescale whatever the bands then say, in BOTH directions; the tool already reports `vacuous` for a demand everybody meets.
remedy.acceptance: tools/quests/critic-attr-scale-souls.mjs exits 0 (i.e. the piece's claim holds after the economy is re-derived) OR the sweep's bought_points equals the measured award divided through levels.json to within one point; AND tools/quests/critic-attr-scale-dtf.mjs reports a non-zero margin_at_hard_cap for every one of the ten attributes, where it currently reports 0 for all ten.

secondary_observations.what: A3 in --after mode cannot fail. The probe sets `root-speech` to 100, then sets the misspelt `root_speech` to 100 WITHOUT resetting the correctly-spelt key first, and setSkills merges — so at the moment A3 reads the gate the real skill is still 100 and the floor is satisfied either way. Both disjuncts of the --after predicate hold unconditionally on fixed data. The claim A3 asserts is true; A3 is not the thing that established it. Reset root-speech to 5 before poking the misspelt key and it becomes a real check.

The round-2 successor corrected its own predecessor's Finding 7. The draft said attributes 'reach nothing inside the fight'; that is false. Four attributes reach combat through the pools on a live path (applyDerivedPools -> derivePools): vigour -> hp_max, endurance -> stamina_max and regen, strength -> equip_load_max, willpower -> focus_max and spell_slots. Willpower additionally reaches spell DAMAGE — engine.js:1581 feeds pools.from.willpower into MagicSystem.setWillpower, and combat-bridge.js:92 computes dmg from M.outputOf(effect, magnitude, M.wil). What is genuinely dead is WEAPON damage: inside game/src/combat/ the only attribute read of any kind is endurance -> staminaMaxFor(), and scalingBonus()/effectiveGrade() are called from nowhere but their own definitions.

Two scaling curves exist and the one that runs is not the one the corpus authored, while its own docstring claims otherwise. magic/system.js:1503 documents 'output = M x output_per_point x (1 + gradeCoeff x scalingBonus(stat))' and then computes (attrValue - 10) / 90 with a hard-coded 0.55 in place of gradeCoeff — a value that is not any entry in GRADE_COEFF (S 1.00 / A 0.80 / B 0.62 / C 0.46 / D 0.32 / E 0.18). Measured against its own stated formula the shipped multiplier is 16-19% low across the mid-range (willpower 30: 1.1222 vs 1.3410 = 0.837; willpower 40: 0.806) and converges at both endpoints, which is precisely the shape an endpoint test cannot see. NOT charged against this piece.

tools/verdict-validate.mjs does not enforce most of its own schema. Mutation-tested with a `none` control and sha256 per row: dropping biggest_gap, emptying artifacts, dropping self_audit, and conflict_of_interest=true with status PASS are all caught (exit 1). But piece_id set to 'NOT A Valid Slug!!' against its pattern, score.overall_0_10 = 99 against maximum 10, and an invented key inside `score` against additionalProperties:false all PASS. So it checks top-level `required` and the two allOf conditionals, and ignores pattern, minimum/maximum and additionalProperties. W1-SOULS-r3.json already carries score.axes and score.confidence_note, which the schema forbids, and the gate reports OK. 'Schema-valid' is therefore a weaker claim than it reads.

The first draft of that mutation table was itself an inert control, and it is recorded because it is the exact failure this verdict fails the builder for. A shell-escaping bug meant the mutation name reached Node as a literal string, no mutation was ever applied, and all seven rows returned 'exit 0 — MISSED', which read as a devastating finding and was a broken instrument measuring nothing. Caught only because the result contradicted a hand run from minutes earlier. The published table now prints a sha256 per row and carries a `none` arm that must validate clean.

attr-scale-audit prints '124 quests, 177 resolutions'. 177 is the count of resolutions carrying at least one stat demand (byResolution.size), not the resolution count — the same report's non-violent block counts 370. A mislabel, not a defect.

The consumption probe hard-codes personality 31 as 'reachable_ceiling.from_max, the best of 240 sheets'. The sweep now says 33. A written-down ceiling inside the probe is precisely what the auditor's own design forbids everywhere else.

check-quests fires correctly and exits 0. Reinjecting personality 45 and `scribing` 35 prints both defects with their bands and measured ceilings plus the non-violent consequence, and the process exits 0. Correct under rule 13 — no fail-closed assertion landed ahead of its data — but the next author to type `personality 40` is warned, not stopped. Worth promoting once the sweep is tracked.

The builder's honesty is above the bar this project normally sees and should be said plainly: it named 14 of the 42 reverted edits as ladder-inversion fixes rather than defects, refusing to bank 42 defect fixes when only 28 were defects; it caught and reported a hole in its own self-test through mutation testing; it ruled the seven `skill: 0` demands NOT a defect with a self-test case on each side of the line; and it recorded the file contention with W1-FACTIONS-r2. None of that is why this verdict fails. It fails on one probe that could not fail.

method_deviations.deviation: The souls-award measurement (10 real kills, 378 souls, red control clean) was taken by this critic run's predecessor at HEAD 6bb9003 and is NOT re-observed by the signing critic. node tools/contention.mjs --gate returned exit 3 twice during the round-2 session (5 instances / 6.04 per core, then 6 instances / 6.72 per core, against ceilings of 6 and 4.0), and the predecessor had already proceeded past exit 3 twice for this same figure.
method_deviations.why: git diff 6bb9003..692bcc8 touches none of game/src/sim/souls.js, game/src/character/derive.js, game/src/sim/magic/system.js or game/data/quests/ — the award path and the judged data are byte-identical between the two commits — so a seventh browser on a saturated box would have re-derived a number that could not have moved. Every OTHER number in this verdict was re-run by the signing critic on HEAD 692bcc8 and is recorded in r2-remeasure.txt. Stated per rule 26 rather than left implicit.

notes:
SCORING, min over axes, no averaging — the axis table the schema's `score` object has no field for.

| Axis | Score | Why |
|---|---:|---|
| A. The defect class was found and fixed | 8 | 42 resolutions; independent revert reproduces 0 -> 23 defects, 0 -> 1 ladder inversion, 370 -> 347 reachable. Wider than the brief (11 dead keys, not 2). |
| B. The classifier is honest in both directions | 7 | The `skill: 0` ruling is right and has a self-test on each side of the line; bands recomputed at run time; exit 2 with no sweep. |
| C. The instrument can go red | 6 | Auditor self-test 21/21, and the builder's own mutation testing found a hole it then closed. But A3-after cannot fail, and the mutations never touched trial C. |
| D. CONSUMPTION (RI-MTH07 / ARBITRATION §3) | 3 | Trials A and B are sound and genuinely coupled. Trial C measured nothing, is not flipped by --after, and is the one every band depends on. |
| E. Reproducibility of the published numbers | 3 | '28 defects -> 0' re-measures as 23 -> 0. The load-bearing input is gitignored. |
| F. The stated root cause | 0 | 'The bought attribute stream is dead / unfundable' is false on HEAD: 10 kills, 378 souls, red control clean. Fail-closed. |
| G. Non-violent floor as reported | 5 | Right denominator, right warning about the insensitive one; wrong label — 'MEETS the 45% bar' from a stat-only predicate. |

min = 0 at axis F, and the verdict is 0.0 FAIL-CLOSED.

The draft of this verdict argued the overall down to 3.0 — axis F is a CLAIM, not a subsystem, and the subsystem it justifies survives its own delete-the-fix. The round-2 successor OVERTURNED that. RI-MTH07 aggregates min-over-axes and its coupling axis is not merely failed, it is UNGATED: trial C could not have returned a bad number because it never ran. Scoring that 3.0 is precisely the move min-over-axes exists to prevent — letting seven working axes carry one that was never measured. SCORING.md fixes an unmeasurable axis at 0 fail-closed, and tools/verdict-validate.mjs said so when this file was validated.

WHAT 0.0 DOES NOT MEAN: it is not a judgement that the work is worthless. The 42-resolution fix is real, wider than its brief, and survives an independent delete-the-fix on a tree that has moved under it (0 -> 23 defects, 0 -> 1 ladder inversion, 370 -> 347 reachable, 19 shut BY a defect). Axes A and H score 8. The 0 records one thing precisely: the gate that was supposed to establish this piece's load-bearing premise had no instrument that could have fired, and the premise is false on HEAD.

REVERSIBLE, and the evidence that reverses it: fix trial C (eid not id, filter kind === 'enemy', step before killing, fail on a thrown kill, flip under --after) and the coupling axis becomes GATED. RI-MTH07 is then scored on a real number rather than fail-closed, and if the re-derived ceilings leave the 42 demands where they are, this piece reaches roughly its axis-A score in one round without a single data edit.

The dispatch brief predicted the failure would be a piece that made attributes a pure damage multiplier. It is the opposite: this piece is almost entirely Morrowind-side, five out-of-combat consumers deep, and the Souls half of attribute scaling is the half that does not exist.
